item.title: Dahl Al Misfar Cave
item.description:
Additional Notes

“One of the more vibrant Qatar attractions for tourists, the 40-meter-deep cave exudes phosphorescence and has a unique beauty. The reason for the glow is a geographical phenomenon known as the “desert rose” (clusters of rose-shaped gypsum crystals) formed from gypsum deposits found in the central part of the peninsula. What is more striking is that the fibrous gypsum forms the depth of the Amisfir Caves up to 40 meters, and sometimes emits a faint moon-like phosphorescence.”

item.title: Musfur Sinkhole
item.description:
Details

Identification

Cave and exploration data

  • Vertical access: No
  • Tourism potential: Medium
  • Goes to water: No

Additional Notes

History of The Musufur Sinkhole in Qatar The Musufur Sinkhole in Qatar occurs with a geological layer called the Upper Dammam Unit. It was formed with the water created a dissolution layer of gypsum, that led to an overlaying stratum of lime-stone to collapse eventually, like any other Karst caves in the Middle East. A layer of Dolomite fell apart with the size of the chamber underneath. It continues to evolve and will in the future as well. Pieces of rock from the dolomite and limestone layers fall and huge sections of the roof could collapse one fine day.
